item.title: every word is a slap
item.description: Tamatha Paul, Green Party MP for Wellington Central in New Zealand (elected 2023). First Māori MP for that seat. The clip is from a late July 2026 debate on a bill making English an official language alongside te reo Māori and NZ Sign Language. She opposed it, calling English a “bastard language” (a mix of others), arguing the focus wastes time amid cost-of-living pressures, and that te reo needs protection after historical suppression. She praised Wales for prioritising Welsh.

item.title: GovBrief Today #547
item.description: A lie about paint put a 67-year-old Olympian in handcuffs. We knew nobody in Ohio was eating cats and dogs, and the vice president admitted he would "create stories" to get attention. We knew a Sharpie stretched that hurricane map into Alabama. And we knew there was no 300-foot gash in the Reflecting Pool. Trump kept lying anyway, and this time the government followed him. Park Police handcuffed Davey Hearn for touching water on a bike ride. A US Attorney announced his felony at a press conference. The truth arrived on a summer Friday afternoon, in a court filing that admits the $14.6 million paint job was "hasty and botched" and that a Park Service engineer flagged the peeling liner eight days before Hearn ever stopped his bike. The government had the answer in its inbox before it had a suspect. Governments lie to keep secrets. This lie kept a president from admitting his paint job failed. I've emailed 8,467 stories over 547 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will.
